state.task: Evaluate five specific execution-contract omissions in CanLang, a compact SaaS language centered on CRUD, policies, rules and workflows. Ease of adoption, economical AI generation and dependable owner-local ordering are the criteria. The alternatives remain draft proposals. Do not presume any option is preferred, add infrastructure or DTO layers, author new business behavior, or infer that compiler/library code has been delivered.
state.facts: Read access in DESIGN §4 is default-denied and assembled from matching row/field grants, subject to fixed identity, team and parent bounds. Before a viewer search, aggregate or serialization, those grants filter its data. Rules inside mutation evaluation may see confidential authoritative state but cannot return it as a caller grant. Pure derive cycles are invalid. What remains open is whether a derive used by policy evaluation sees filtered or authority rows: the sample CompanyRole policy reaches has_role, which itself scans CompanyRole. Ordinary read=true uses viewer visibility; the existing scope=authority declaration is an intentional typed output grant. DESIGN §§3 and 5–7 require record versions at mutation admission, ordered effects in proposed state, pre-write locks, final validation and a single commit owner. Hook before and input are read-only, after is mutable, and changing after never invokes its own CRUD again. Scenario writes leave CRUD hooks out. Fixture rows use initial version 1. §11 already distinguishes one revision per converted row from rename-only preservation; business assignments and no-ops have no corresponding precise rule. Source schedules reveal ordinary records using version+1 after set, unlike hooks using after.version directly.
state.workflow: Every(duration) in §6 has UTC epoch alignment and one coalesced current tick after missed periods. Trusted invocations carry verified routing context and no actor, but the draft omits tenant and storage-instance selection for these ticks. Team-owned D1 is the default, and each bound Durable Object root has its own SQLite authority. Eventual directory entries only discover roots; they cannot decide availability. Atomic business queries and mutations cannot span owners under §7; bounded fencing/retry includes receipts, history and delivery intents. All false require checks reject under §5, whereas §6 names a false handler guard skipped. GRAMMAR reuses require on either side of do. The actual CanStats trusted example demands rule_failed for failed leading checks, while handlers can also fail checks amid effects. Existing cancellation/supersession and dispatch when=false are distinct skip cases. The closed DeliveryResult status enum is pending/succeeded/failed/unknown/skipped and its DeliveryError has safe code/message; additional outcome types would duplicate the current surface.
state.files: Within §8, selected file use implies the application’s one R2 store. References denote checked, finished, immutable content. Type/content, maximum length and quota are enforced before attachment, which needs current app/team/principal ownership or a readable prior attachment. IDs and URLs alone are insufficient. Typed remote results nevertheless can carry file into a later authoritative completion handler; the supplied quote/invoice sources assign their returned PDF under the shown real by/rule/correlation facts. Such handlers have actor=null, and delivery verification does not itself prove receiving file authorization. Completed unattached content already has bounded cleanup after retry/attachment needs. The adapter implementation supplies authenticated transport and explicit mappings; do not fabricate language functions or change the quotation app’s absent revision match.
state.research: The PostgreSQL primary manual allows policy expressions evaluated with user rights and privileged access through security-definer functions; it demonstrates that the two privilege approaches have genuine implications. The SQLite primary manual governs SQL transaction outcomes without assigning CanLang metadata versions. No external manual certifies these proposed semantics or their unimplemented execution. Documentation: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/ddl-rowsecurity.html and https://www.sqlite.org/lang_transaction.html
state.instruction: Choose among each question’s specified options without suppressing an unresolved answer. Separately classify whether their authority, write-intent, per-scope tick, uniform rejection and receiver-finalization combination is internally coherent. Report uncertainty normally; a common classifier selection is neither user authorization nor a successful runtime test.

code.draft/CanCustomer.can:24-36:
export derive has_role(person:user,org:Customer,role:CompanyRole.role):bool = any(org.CompanyRole as grant,grant.account==person and grant.role==role and grant.active)
  export derive has_location_role(person:user,org:Customer,role:CompanyRole.role,location:Location):bool = any(org.CompanyRole as grant,grant.account==person and grant.role==role and grant.active and location in grant.locations)
  export derive owns(person:user,org:Customer):bool = org.kind==individual and any(org.Contact as contact,contact.account==person and contact.verified)
  derive customer_staff(person:user,org:Customer):bool = any(org.locations as location,can_work(person,location))
  policy Customer read=customer_reader or billing_reader where=customer_staff(actor,row) fields=name,kind,locations,active
  policy Customer read=customer_manager and customer_staff(actor,row)
  policy Customer read=authenticated where=owns(actor,row) or has_role(actor,row,administrator) or has_role(actor,row,booker) or has_role(actor,row,billing)
  policy Contact read=authenticated where=actor.email_verified and row.email==actor.email fields=name,email,account,verified
  policy Contact read=customer_reader or billing_reader where=customer_staff(actor,row.parent) fields=name,email,phone,verified
  policy Contact read=customer_manager and customer_staff(actor,row.parent)
  policy Contact read=authenticated where=row.account==actor or has_role(actor,row.parent,administrator)
  policy CompanyRole read=authenticated where=row.account==actor or has_role(actor,row.parent,administrator)
  policy CompanyRole read=customer_manager and customer_staff(actor,row.parent)
code.draft/CanStats.can:33-47:
scenario process on=WebJobs
   require event.site.active and event.occurred<=now+5m and event.occurred>now-30d
   do
    if not any(event.site.AcceptedEvent as accepted,accepted.event_id==event.event_id)
     create AcceptedEvent {parent=event.site,event_id=event.event_id,name=event.name,occurred=event.occurred,path=event.path,location=event.location,workspace=event.workspace,source=event.source,medium=event.medium,visitor=event.visitor,session=event.session,session_started=event.session_started} as accepted
     send WebDimensions.write {site=event.site.id,name=event.name,path=event.path,location=event.location,source=event.source,value=1} as telemetry
     for health in event.site.Health limit=1
      set health {accepted=health.accepted+1,last_processed=now}
   examples seed=[health] event=WebEvent {site=website,event_id="fresh",name="page_view",occurred=now,path="/"}
    website.active -> health.accepted
    true -> 1
    false -> error(rule_failed)
   examples seed=[health] event=WebEvent {site=website,event_id="expired",name="page_view",occurred=now-30d,path="/"}
    website.active -> health.accepted
    true -> error(rule_failed)
code.draft/CanBook.can:95-104:
scenario ready on=every(1m)
   do
    for appointment in Appointment as item where item.state==pending and item.host_ok and item.room_ok limit=100
     set appointment {state=confirmed}
     send Mail.send {to=appointment.contact.email,subject=format("Appointment confirmed"@{nl="Afspraak bevestigd"},locale=null),body=appointment.parent.parent.instructions} as confirmation
     if appointment.from>now+1h
      schedule appointment.id at=appointment.from-1h event=Reminder {appointment,revision=appointment.version+1}
  scenario remind on=Reminder
   require event.appointment.state==confirmed and event.appointment.version==event.revision
   do send Mail.send {to=event.appointment.contact.email,subject=format("Appointment reminder"@{nl="Afspraakherinnering"},locale=null),body=event.appointment.parent.parent.instructions} when=event.appointment.state==confirmed as notice
code.draft/CanPropose.can:66-75:
scenario document(revision:Revision) by=salesperson or authenticated label=label_QuotePdf_document
   require revision.state in [sent,accepted,declined] and ((salesperson and can_work(actor,revision.parent.location)) or (actor.email_verified and actor.email==revision.recipient_email))
   do
    send Documents.quote {source=revision.id,revision=revision.version,snapshot=QuoteDocument {issuer=revision.issuer_snapshot,recipient=revision.recipient_email,title=revision.title_snapshot,location=revision.location_snapshot,from=revision.from,until=revision.until,terms=revision.terms,expires=revision.expires,lines=revision.Item as item select QuoteLine {title=item.title,quantity=item.quantity,price=item.price,tax=item.tax,discount=item.discount},total=revision.total}} as delivery
    set revision {document_delivery=delivery.id}
  scenario document_result on=Documents.quote.completed
   do
    for revision in Revision as row where row.document_delivery==event.delivery_id limit=1
     if event.status==succeeded and event.result?.source==revision.id
      set revision {pdf=event.result.document}
code.draft/CanInvoice.can:118-126:
require invoice.state==issued and invoice.number!=null and invoice.issued_at!=null and (owns(actor,invoice.parent) or has_role(actor,invoice.parent,billing) or (finance and can_work(actor,invoice.location)))
   do
    send Documents.invoice {source=invoice.id,revision=invoice.version,snapshot=InvoiceDocument {issuer=invoice.issuer,recipient=invoice.recipient,address=invoice.address,tax_reference=invoice.tax_reference,number=invoice.number,issued_at=invoice.issued_at,due=invoice.due,currency=invoice.currency,lines=invoice.Line as line select DocumentLine {title=line.description,quantity=line.quantity,price=line.price,tax=line.tax,discount=line.discount},credits=invoice.Credit as credit select DocumentCredit {amount=credit.amount,reason=credit.reason},payments=invoice.Attempt as payment select DocumentPayment {reference=payment.reference,amount=payment.amount,state=format("{status}",{status=payment.status}),received=payment.received},total=invoice.total}} as delivery
    create DocumentRequest {parent=invoice,revision=invoice.version,delivery=delivery.id} as request
  scenario document_result on=Documents.invoice.completed
   do
    for request in DocumentRequest as row where row.delivery==event.delivery_id limit=1
     if event.status==succeeded and event.result?.source==request.parent.id and event.result.revision==request.revision
      create Document {parent=request.parent,revision=request.revision,file=event.result.document} as document

policy.instructions: Which bounded data visibility should a policy-evaluation derive use?

criteria.authority: Allow authority-state inspection for policy grants and for invariant, lock, CRUD-when and mutation/trusted decision expressions. Preserve owner, team, parent and lifetime restrictions. Pure derives inherit this evaluation mode; viewer outputs and ordinary read scenarios still enforce dependency grants, with existing scope=authority for intentional disclosure. Underlying grant scans bypass policy reentry, never the prohibition on pure recursion. This enables current role-table authorization, but requires a strict decision/output privilege boundary.
criteria.viewer: Give policy queries the same filtered view as caller-facing queries and reject cycles in policy dependencies. A single visibility rule limits authority exposure, although the supplied CompanyRole recursion then becomes invalid or needs new app read grants and hidden role rows cannot govern access.
criteria.unresolved: Wait for an owner-bounded role-check example before selecting either privilege interpretation. The uncertainty is retained at the cost of incomplete permission evaluation.

versions.instructions: Which consistent revision model best fits the shown scenarios and hooks?

criteria.write_intent: Hold newly inserted metadata at 1. For a preexisting record, ordinary version reads remain its admitted v while value reads follow provisional effects. Any accepted set/update/archive target, including an unchanged assignment, advances once to v+1 at commit; hook after exposes that planned v+1 and before exposes v. Further writes, calls and hook adjustments share one advancement/change-history event, while merely referenced parents or send-only records are untouched. It avoids rewrites of current +1 and hook schedules, but raises revisions and audit output on no-ops.
criteria.live_dirty: On the first effective normalized change, switch an old row’s visible revision to v+1 in both aliases and hook after. Keep it fixed through later changes or reversions; equal-only writes leave v and new records use 1. This reduces no-op conflicts and aligns versions with provisional value reads, but requires replacing current post-set +1 uses and correctly tracking edit state through hooks.
criteria.unresolved: Keep the revision contract provisional until ordered mutation examples resolve creation, equal assignments and hook edits. Such caution leaves event and reminder version binding underspecified.

ticks.instructions: Determine how epoch ticks should select an owner and tenant.

criteria.per_scope: Infer a unique scope family from owner-anchored queries/mutations and dispatch one occurrence for each active D1 team, once for app-only handlers, or for each authoritative root instance when root-bound. Each transaction reads only that scope; incompatible combinations are errors. Record handler/release, owner/team and epoch in the occurrence identity, coalesce separately, and start a new scope with the subsequent epoch. This preserves short recurring app sources, but demands correct authoritative fanout enumeration rather than relying on eventual discovery.
criteria.d1_first: Limit automatic recurrence to inferred D1 team/app scopes for v1; root-targeted or mixed scopes fail checking and can use the existing record-specific schedule primitive. This narrows coverage and isolation obligations, while root authors must explicitly arm work and cannot rely on unrestricted every.
criteria.unresolved: Keep every routing undecided until concrete coverage and owner-isolation evidence is available. This avoids claiming automatic fanout prematurely, while acknowledging that current recurring source lacks a runnable tenant context.

requires.instructions: Select the observable rejection-versus-skip rule for verified handlers.

criteria.business_error: A false require always aborts provisional work and yields its safe business error, default rule_failed, regardless of whether it precedes do. Persist a terminal failed occurrence; reserve retries for runtime transients. Cancellation, supersession, lifecycle expiry/invalidation and failed dispatch when produce skipped. Inline BDD reaches the same real rejection path. This preserves one primitive and current Stats errors, but expected stale timers contribute failed outcomes.
criteria.leading_skip: A trusted require preceding do ends the occurrence as skipped when false; checks during do instead fail with a business error and rollback. BDD observes skipped for the former and changes the two Stats expectations. This distinguishes stale preconditions from body rejection, with the drawback that moving identical checks across do changes semantics.
criteria.unresolved: Do not claim either contradictory outcome rule is final; seek a concrete terminal disposition choice first. The cost is that the trusted examples and execution contract cannot yet agree.

files.instructions: Determine the minimal valid handoff for remote file-valued completions.

criteria.receiver_finalize: Finish checked immutable bytes through the consumer app’s established upload flow before publishing successful completion. Retain internal delivery/path-bound provenance for receiving app, tenant and owner, initiating principal or trusted source, and adapter. Only its verified completion can attach those bytes under this authority, without forging actor. A replay uses the same finalized object and conflicting content fails; local rollback leaves normal orphan cleanup, never a cross-store atomic promise. PDF source contracts continue to work but need copying, quota accounting and real adapter finalization.
criteria.provider_reference: Accept a retained immutable provider reference only with verified delegated access, attachment permission and lifetime/download guarantees. This may avoid moving bytes into local storage, at the expense of adding remote file authority and retention semantics; unverified IDs and URLs still confer nothing.
criteria.reject_remote_file: Reject capabilities returning file until receiving authorization is defined. This is a smaller enforceable boundary, but prevents compilation of the present PDF result contracts unless their workflows change.
criteria.unresolved: Leave the existing remote-file shape explicitly pending rather than disguising an authorization gap. It retains flexibility but supplies no executable attachment handoff.

coherence.instructions: Can the authority predicates, fixed admission versions with write-intent advancement, isolated tick fanout, uniform require errors and recipient file finalization coexist under the current source and permission constraints?

criteria.true: The bundle is semantically consistent with the evidence, preserving order and owner/read limits while admitting that runtime support is absent.
criteria.false: The combination contains an identifiable incompatibility that must be corrected; favorable isolated choices cannot establish overall coherence.
